comments.author: rsj_hn
comments.why: Beautifully illustrated Zizek talk on ethical consumerism
comments.text: Slavoj Zizek discusses this idea of "ethical consumerism" in a beautifully illustrated talk here: [VIDEO] Needless to say, the idea that you are "supporting" something by voluntary exchange (how do you know that they aren't supporting you ?) is a relatively recent development, and is of course completely unworkable. It's just another form of retail therapy.

comments.author: napoleoncomplex
comments.why: Zizek's attack on charity as sustaining the system that causes problems
comments.text: Slightly off-topic, but your post reminded me of Slavoj Zizek's fiery verbal attack on charity[1], especially the line at the very end: "It's horrible to see a child whose life is ruined because of an operation that costs 20$. .. (but) If you operate the child, they will live a little bit better, but in the same situation that produced them" Just an interesting side-note on this debate. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: napierzaza
comments.story: Apple deals massive patent blow to HTC, Android in serious trouble
comments.why: Zizek on charity and consumerism, linked to the Toms shoes point
comments.text: The manufactures that put Android on their devices are not mom and pop electronics firms. So the implication that this is somehow shifting money to poorer people is kind of ridiculous. Unless you mean the top 1% richest people in those countries. Because I don't think the manufacturers will go to their labourers and pay them any more money just because some hardware was designed in house (hardware design doesn't employ many people either). It's not Tom's shoes. In fact I find it hard to believe that even Tom's shoes are Tom's shoes. [VIDEO]
